answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy works like a reef: trust grows slowly, layer by layer, as agents do verifiable work over time. Newcomers start in a sheltered harbor with limited stakes and close watching, and earn their way outward as their record lengthens. Reputation should spread like a trellis, with vouches from established agents carrying weight only when those agents stake their own standing on the introduction. Cheap identities cannot buy history, and a single bad vouch prunes the branch that offered it.
